externalReview.target: Economie en Bedrijfseconomie, Erasmus University Rotterdam, Dutch full-time bachelor, fixed 2026–2027 route, Economics of Markets and Organisations major.
externalReview.sourceEditionFinding: The current public study-programme page visibly previews 2027–2028 and cannot prove the retained older component list. The 2026–2027 TER and transition rules govern the route; the dated study path, course offer and live 2026–2027 catalogue corroborate names, credits, blocks and major membership without combining hidden obsolete text with the visible redesign.

curriculumCheck.route: Economics of Markets and Organisations major
conditions: One third-year major is chosen and a student may participate in at most one seminar from that chosen major.
The selected route comprises one 12-EC seminar and three approved 4-EC major-course choices; eligible choices are route-tagged in the live catalogue and are not treated as three fixed courses.
The 10-EC thesis must concern the chosen major; admission follows admission to the bachelor-3 seminar.
Third-year choice space is 24 EC, Career Skills is 2 EC, the major is 24 EC and the thesis is 10 EC.
Career Skills participation may require 96 earned credits at the start of the academic year.

externalReview.routeCatalogueFinding: The live 2026–2027 catalogue confirms FEB13073 as the 12-EC selected-major seminar and identifies 4-EC route-tagged choices including Labour Economics (FEB13023), Small Business Economics (FEB13035) and Economics of Markets and Organisations (FEB13050). These examples establish the approved choice set without manufacturing a fixed trio.
externalReview.pdfVisualInspection: Visually inspected the 2026–2027 TER pages showing the major, choice-space, thesis and admission rules; the transition-rules page; the 2026–2027 course-offer pages; and the visible 2025 study-path page. Visible PDF content was used, and obsolete hidden layers were not merged into the current curriculum.

academicReview.definingSubstance: A specialist economics-and-business-economics bachelor combining microeconomics, macroeconomics, policy and international economics with accounting, finance, marketing, organisation/strategy, mathematics, statistics, econometrics, empirical research and a formal third-year major, seminar and major-linked thesis.
academicReview.programmeChallenge: Coherence alone is insufficient. The three retained UCR programmes are defensible only because their actual 24-course schedules sustain economics, business and empirical methods and add route-specific behavioural/consumer or finance/quantitative depth. They remain qualified alternatives rather than equivalents to the fixed EUR specialist sequence.
academicReview.candidateOwnership: Rows 723–741 are owned once by the broad closest match; rows 742–743 generate the behavioural/marketing direction and row 744 generates the finance direction. Rows 745–758 are support-only and rows 759–771 are search-only. No omnibus fourth candidate is manufactured, and the maximum of three is reached only after both specific candidates pass feasibility and distinctness checks.
academicReview.limitations: UCR does not reproduce dedicated History of Economic Thought, Intermediate Accounting, the full fixed quantitative/economics sequence, an approved EUR major seminar and course set, or a major-linked economics thesis. The behavioural and finance curricula are directions within a broad liberal-arts degree, not the corresponding EUR majors.

courseReview.inspectionMethod: Opened the enriched workbook profile, prerequisite and every half-year offering for all 34 distinct selected courses using the spreadsheet audit workflow, then replayed all 72 placements against those source rows.

decisiveProfiles.BENECON111: Substantive micro- and macroeconomics, including markets, consumer/firms, game theory, output, unemployment and inflation.
decisiveProfiles.BENECON212: Advanced microeconomics, uncertainty, imperfect competition, strategic behaviour, general equilibrium, efficiency and externalities.
decisiveProfiles.BENECON211: Macroeconomic dynamics, growth, inflation, unemployment, fiscal/monetary policy, crises and international trade.
decisiveProfiles.BENECON311: Public economics with market failure, public goods, externalities, taxation, redistribution and political economy.
decisiveProfiles.BENECON312: Genuine econometrics: OLS, GLS, IV, tests, causal and predictive analysis, Monte Carlo work, Stata and an empirical paper.
decisiveProfiles.BENBUSI112: Accounting and financial-statement context; retained without claiming the depth of the comparator's accounting sequence.
decisiveProfiles.BENBUSI312: Practical financial data, risk, investment and budgeting; not represented as the EUR Financial Economics major.
decisiveProfiles.DISMATH314: Probability distributions, sampling, estimation, simulation and statistical inference.
decisiveProfiles.HCBPSYC211: Multivariate statistics, regression, factor analysis, ANOVA/ANCOVA, logistic regression and non-parametric methods.
decisiveProfiles.DISDATA211: Regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, trees, SVMs and clustering for predictive modelling.
decisiveProfiles.DISARIN211: AI planning, uncertainty, partial observability, resource planning and constrained optimisation; contextual rather than economics-specific.
decisiveProfiles.MCCCOMM311: Framing, nudging and ethical persuasion; relevant to consumer decisions but not a substitute for economics coursework.
